content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now, starting with the symptom: account pages were failing for many shoppers. Next I'm working through the causal chain, beginning with the server errors shoppers saw on their account page requests.

Next I'm writing out the cause step: the monthly-spend flag was switched on at P1, which sent account page requests down the new code path. The logs show it partly on by 03:46 and fully on from 03:47. I'm also checking whether any deploys happened in the window, and none turned up in the day's read.

Now I'm checking the last place a change could have come from: a deployment in the window, which the day's read didn't surface. Next I'm settling the root cause, which is the function the flag turned on. It divides by the count of this month's purchases, and for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month that count is zero. That reading rests on the code and the flag history rather than a run of the failing case, though the error at that line in the logs matches it.

I'm settling on the root cause now: the average-spend function divides by this month's purchase count without guarding against zero, so any shopper with no purchases this month hits a ZeroDivisionError at line 47 once the flag routes the account page through it.

Still weighing whether the flag's gradual rollout was a factor: the logs show about half of traffic switched over at 03:46 and everything from 03:47, with no staged rollout in view.

I'm now looking at the contributing factors: the flag went to all traffic at once, with no staged rollout or error-rate gate in view, and I'm checking whether any test covered a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on.

Now I'm weighing whether the contributing factors need their own items: the flag went to all traffic at once with no staged rollout or automatic halt, and no test was seen covering a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on.

Now I'm drafting the action items: a staged rollout for flag changes, an automatic halt when error rates rise, and a test requirement covering shoppers with no purchases this month before any flag goes on in production.

I'm working out the postmortem's remaining items now: the proposed follow-ups, including whether the function should keep raising for accounts with no purchases at all, which the current tests seem to expect. Then I'll turn to what went well, like the investigator tying the flag change to the errors and the mitigation reverting it.

I'm noting the proposed fix PR as a draft, and that the revert itself could be undone if needed. Nothing else in this part of the review points to a separate mistake beyond the unchecked flag switch I already have as a contributing factor. The timing of the onset at 03:46 rests on the flag change, but the empty-purchase-list mechanism is still Code-Fix's reading rather than something I've seen run.

I'm laying out the causal chain in order: first the shoppers' account page errors, then the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47 that began when the flag went on, and then the switch itself. Next comes the root cause, stated as a single sentence.

I'm ruling out a deployment in the window, since the read-back of production changes showed only the flag switch and no deploy. The provider history also shows that flag change was the only one anyone made in that hour apart from Argus. The client-disconnect errors were already happening at their usual rate before the onset, and only the ZeroDivisionError appears from the minute the flag went on.

I'm weighing how to phrase the file location: naming the file and the line the logs point to is enough, without the bare line number. For the pull request, I'll just say "a draft pull request" rather than citing its number. And the went-well items should each open with the agent that did the thing.

action_items.item: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, starting with a small share of traffic, instead of switching them on for all traffic at once.
Halt and revert a staged flag rollout automatically when the service's error rate rises while it is under way.
Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including for shoppers with no purchases in the current month, to pass before that flag can be switched on in production.
Decide whether `average_spend_per_item`, used while the flag is off, should keep raising for an account with no purchases at all. Code-Fix reports that the current tests expect it to raise.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers opening their account page got a failed request instead of the page, and the service's share of failed requests rose sharply.

Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero, raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The error shows up in the logs from the minute the flag went on until the logs that were read end.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: the production change events read back for the day before the onset held only this flag change, and no deploy came back.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read, and that was this one.

The client-disconnect failures on the account page: these were seen before the onset, while the account page error rate was still low. The division-by-zero failures appear only from the minute the flag went on.

causal_chain.step: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. The flag's evaluations went from all off to a mix of on and off within that minute, and to all on from the next minute.

With the flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a new monthly per-item average that divides by the number of this month's purchases, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new feature made the account page use a new monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month because it ends up dividing by zero.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag switch reached all of the account page's traffic at once: its evaluations went from all off to all on within about a minute. No staged rollout and no error-rate check that would halt it were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that halted when errors rose would have exposed only a small share of shoppers, and would have been stopped before it reached all traffic.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no test was seen that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases in the current month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have raised the division by zero before the flag was turned on, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed a single candidate, C1, which tied the division-by-zero failures to the flag switch.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off, a change that can be undone.
The Mitigation Agent judged the revert confirmed once the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix, with tests, as a draft pull request for a person to review.

input.root_cause: The function the flag turned on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, divides the account's total spent this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month` and has no answer for an empty list. For any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError at the line the logs name, so every account page request for such a shopper failed once monthly-spend-feature sent the page's spend figure through it.
input.still_at_risk: Code-Fix's reading says the faulty calculation was still in the code: switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month, and with the flag off, the older calculation can still fail for accounts with no purchases at all.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
